correctness.rationale: For each allowed force value, exact generator substitution verifies LΦ=µ−(U²−kXU). Both force processes have identical covariance v²exp(−g|t|)/2 and stationary mixed moments E[XU]=v²/[2(k+g)] and E[X²]=v²/[2k(k+g)]. Evaluated finite-jump compensators, including both rest-to-run signs, yield V3=gv⁴/[4(k+g)²] and V2=gkv⁴/[2(k+g)³]. Bounded stationary coordinate, bounded correctors and jump sizes, ergodic brackets and the martingale central limit theorem give rigorous variance rate and Gaussian scaling for every positive k,g,v. Exact symbolic checks and event-driven results on six parameter sets agree; the experiment alone is not used as proof.

value.rationale: A natural physical model-identification problem asks whether stationary second-order displacement data and mean power determine energetic reliability. A matched pair of non-Gaussian motility mechanisms has identical complete second-order force/position statistics and mean power, yet their work variances reverse order at the physically meaningful switching-to-trap ratio one. Exact strict inequalities, unique noise maxima at g=k and g=k/2, and distinct high-switching powers g^{-1} versus g^{-2} provide structural, experimentally interpretable discrimination. This resolves a motivated gap about mechanical-work noise rather than reprinting static moments or an arbitrary parameter slice.
